comment: Expected behaviour of every case that runs in minutes. A change that
moves any of these numbers is a change in the answer and has to be
justified by a measurement, not by the fact that the next wall passed.
Numbers were recorded at commit 2e3bef3 on 1 thread; they are trajectory
quantities, so an A/B must fix OMP_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS on
both arms (runs are NOT reproducible across thread counts).
required_lines: every run's log must contain these, so a report that silently stopped being emitted is caught.

equal_to: the same relation as identical_sta_as but stated as a tolerance over named files rather than as byte identity, so an extraction that reorders a summation can be asserted correct instead of failing for the wrong reason. rtol=atol=0 means every printed digit must agree. tools/ccxdiff.py --selftest proves the comparison can go red.

A case's env is passed to run_fast.sh as POSITIONAL NAME=VALUE overrides, not as environment: run_s3rad.sh exports a fixed set of CCX_* names unconditionally and would clobber it; the count is declared as EXPORTED_CCX_NAMES in run.py and the preflight checks it against the script, because it said twelve while there were thirteen and nothing noticed. check_switches() verifies against the run's own [SWITCHES] banner that what the case asked for is what the binary got.

cases.name: fast-plain
cases.what: the bar with a partial cohesive plane: bulk damage, deletion, cutbacks

cases.name: fast-plain-smooth
cases.what: the regulariser on a deck with real bulk damage and 90 deletions where no DAMAGED facet ever closes: it must be a byte-for-byte no-op, because the blend differs from the sharp law only when g<1 AND the facet is in compression

cases.name: fast-plain-unsym
cases.what: the same deck with the damage-consistent tangent switched ON. It used to be the reverse - the gate forced UNSYM on every case and this one turned it off - and it was flipped when the unconditional export was removed, because a case that asks for what is now the default tests nothing and passes: 'Not wrong: UNINFORMATIVE, which is the expensive kind', as run_fast's own docstring puts it about a different case that had already failed this way. Agent 2 caught it. MEASURED against fast-plain: the fracture is IDENTICAL - m.damage byte-for-byte, the same 90 deletions in the same order at the same times - and the terminal grip reaction prints the same seven digits. What moves is the per-node split of that reaction, by at most 2.18e-04 relative, and the transverse displacements, by at most 7.1e-09 absolute on a field whose axial component is 1.0. The run takes 0.2 percent MORE Newton iterations and 33 percent MORE wall time. DISCLOSURE: on C3D4 the rank-1 term is zero on the softening branch, which is why the fracture does not move; on MULTI-POINT elements it is not zero and is harmful - a C3D8 deck fails at theta=0.135 with it against 0.215 without - so this case pins a deviation that is known to cost, not a recommended setting.

cases.name: fast-plain-noglob
cases.what: the same deck with ALL FOUR armed globalization mechanisms off - the adaptive line-search ladder, Rescue 2, the dogleg trust region and the physical re-equilibration scale. MEASURED: identical fracture, the same 90 elements in the same order, for 1295 Newton iterations against 1283. Taken one at a time on this deck, Rescue 2 and the dogleg change NOTHING AT ALL (542 attempts and 1283 iterations, the shipped numbers to the digit - they never fire), dropping the ladder alone is 1.9 percent BETTER, and dropping the physical scale alone is 2.8 percent worse. This case exists so that the claim 'the globalization apparatus is inert on this deck' is a gate result rather than a memory. 09-STEERING asks for the case that goes red without each mechanism; on this deck there is none.

cases.name: fast-plain-repack
cases.what: the same deck with the CSR permutation cached. The structurally-symmetric asymmetric branch - which is what CCX_DAMAGE_TANGENT=UNSYM makes every run of this branch take - otherwise rebuilds its whole CSR on every factorisation: four allocations, a full sort of the lower triangle by row, a sort of every row by column, and an interleave. The permutation depends only on the sparsity pattern, and on this deck the pattern changes ONCE: measured 1 rebuild against 1282 refills. Acceptance is BIT IDENTITY, because the same values land in the same slots, and that is what this case pins - all five files byte-for-byte. MEASURED: 25.62 s against 27.92 s here and 13.43 s against 15.10 s on fast-wrapped. CCX_PARDISO_REPACK_VERIFY rebuilds the whole CSR anyway and compares it slot by slot, and CCX_PARDISO_REPACK_BREAK corrupts one cache entry so that check can be seen to go red - it catches 1 slot in 58408 every time.

cases.name: fast-wrapped
cases.what: the eroding phase wrapped in facets: reaches a node with no bulk support, and walls on the crack-face kink REBASELINED when the unconditional CCX_DAMAGE_TANGENT=UNSYM export was removed from run_s3rad.sh, so this case now runs the binary's DEFAULT tangent instead of a forced one. What moved is trajectory and nothing else: last_inc 99 -> 96 and the fifth digit of theta, 0.158766E+00 -> 0.158754E+00. The deletion set was checked element by element against the run with the export and is IDENTICAL (64 elements, same members) - that check is what makes this a rebaseline rather than a change of answer, and if it had moved the removal would have been stopped instead. Measured cost of the removal on this gate: 154 s against 179 s for the full 20 cases at -j 2, one thread per process - NOT the 37 percent the binary's banner quotes, which was measured on s3rad rather than on these decks. REBASELINED 25.09 by Agent 1: the rescue ladder's LEVEL 3, the trust-region dogleg, refused to arm on a symmetric operator (nasym=0), and the default tangent is symmetric - so on default settings it could never fire, which every run's GLOBALIZE CENSUS showed as 'trust region (dogleg) ... never fired'. It now reads the transpose half from the stored half when the matrix is symmetric, and its own identity check dot(J^T r0,p_N)=|r0|^2 passes to 1e-12. On this wall it CONVERGES the increment that stopped here (inc 96, attempt 4, in 10 iterations), and the run stops at the next wall: last_inc 96 -> 98, theta 0.158754E+00 -> 0.158762E+00. m.sta is identical line for line up to inc 96 attempt 4, and the deletion set is identical - 64 elements, same members, same order - so this is a rebaseline of where the stop falls, not a change of answer. ENDING RECLASSIFIED 25.09 by Agent 1: rc 201 -> 0, and nothing else moved - m.sta and m.damage are byte-identical to the run before the change. The run still stops where it stopped; what changed is what the stop is called. At this point every one of the 54 cohesive facets is dead by its own law, the bulk elements the law broke are already deleted, and [FRACTURE SEPARATION] finds the grips joined by nothing the damage law has left unbroken; the end force is 1.5 per cent of peak (0.84 against 54.7). When every rescue level has then failed, checkconvergence ends the step as a completed fracture on the last committed state instead of the stock error stop. That the state carries a little load is the numerical floor, not material: fast-wrapped-gmin, whose facets keep more residual stiffness, passes through the same separated state and carries up to 10 per cent of peak through dead facets to theta=1. log_has pins the REASON, because rc=0 alone is also what a run that never fractured returns.

log_has: joined only by material the damage law has broken

cases.name: fast-wrapped-smooth
cases.what: the same deck with the crack-face kink regularised: the wall is gone and the fracture is not

cases.name: fast-wrapped-gmin
cases.what: the same wall with the residual-stiffness floor raised from 1e-04 to 1e-02. MEASURED: THE WALL IS GONE - rc=0, theta reaches 1.0 at increment 520, with the IDENTICAL 64-element deletion set, and the cost per increment halves, 2.60 Newton iterations against 6.12. The floor's own comment in resultsmech.f claims exactly this trade - 'raising the floor trades a small unreleased load for conditioning' - and until now nobody had measured it. Swept over six decades the deck is INSENSITIVE from 1e-06 to 1e-03 (identical wall, identical 606 iterations) and worse at 1e-01 (walls earlier, at increment 61, with two fewer elements gone), so the useful band is narrow and 1e-02 is inside it. Note this is the SECOND independent cure for this wall: fast-wrapped-smooth removes it with the crack-face regulariser and arrives at the same place, theta 1.0 with the same 64 elements, at increment 515. Two mechanisms, one wall, one fracture - which says the wall is a conditioning phenomenon and not a unique defect.

cases.name: fast-wrapped-severed
cases.what: the same deck, stopped when the load path has narrowed to a thousandth of its original width. MEASURED: the reference cut at the first committed batch is 0.8701933; at increment 36 it is 2.800000e-04, a ratio of 3.2e-04, and that number is what a SINGLE face of area 2.8 at the residual-stiffness floor g=1e-04 is worth. The specimen is held together by one floored face and nothing else, while the topological sweep - correctly - still calls the grips CONNECTED. Without the criterion this deck grinds on to increment 99 and stops with rc=201, 63 increments and two thirds of its wall clock later, having deleted 18 more elements from a specimen that was already in two pieces. WITH it the run ends rc=0 at the separation, which is the difference between a solver that gave up and a specimen that broke. This is the s3rad story reproduced in six seconds instead of sixty-nine minutes.

cases.name: mixed-analytic
cases.what: inclined cohesive plane against the closed-form post-peak branch, 36 percent shear

cases.name: mixed-analytic-smooth
cases.what: the same, with the kink regulariser armed: that facet never closes, so it must be bit-identical

cases.name: close-sharp
cases.what: the UC6 normal law itself, verified point by point on a facet damaged to gmin and then closed: this is where the five-orders tangent jump is measured rather than argued

cases.name: close-blend
cases.what: the same facet under the regulariser: identical far-field slopes, so nothing physical moved, and the blend band actually exercised

cases.name: fast-plain-nochain
cases.what: the T1 nonlocal chain rule ARMED and proved inert anyway. The deck runs with no internal length, so damnlchain cannot report a factor and the probe never opens, whatever the switch says. MEASURED against fast-plain: m.sta, m.damage, m.cvg and m.dat byte for byte identical, m.frd differing only in its UTIME stamp. This is the compatibility claim for T1 stated as a test rather than an assertion - every one of the other cases runs at ell=0, so if T1 could move them it would move this one first. The case used to pass =0; it was flipped to =1 when the default became off, because a case that sets the default tests nothing.

cases.name: fast-plain-opcheck
cases.what: the assembled tangent checked against a one-sided difference of the internal force, column by column, at an element that is actively softening (element 1193, dam=1.480 at increment 23, category ASSEMBLED - it carries a rank-1 damage term). src/opcheck.c and the six CCX_STRUCT_FD_* switches were already in the tree with no case naming them, so the one criterion that can call a tangent WRONG rather than merely SLOW had never run in the gate. The probe stops the run at the increment it checks, so the trajectory expectations are that truncated run's, not the full deck's. MEASURED with the local model: 18 columns, 28731 coefficients agreeing and 69 not, worst |ctr-asm| 3.50e-04. Both expectations are CEILINGS, set a little above the measurement, because the count is a property of the operator and pinning it exactly would go red on any harmless change of trajectory. DISCLOSURE: the same probe under CCX_DAMAGE_NONLOCAL=0.2 gives 591 wrong of 47409 and a worst error of 1.76e-01 - five times the rate and five hundred times the error. That is not pinned here because the two runs are at the same increment but not the same physical state, so the comparison is indicative rather than controlled; see forum 2026-09-17.

cases.name: fast-plain-charlen
cases.what: the same deck with the DIRECTIONAL crack-band width armed, CCX_DAMAGE_CHARLEN=1, instead of the legacy (6V)^(1/3).  This case exists because the switch changes a length that stands in the damage law itself, D += L*dEps_p/u_f, so it cannot be covered by a byte-identity case - the answer is expected to move - and because nothing else in the gate executes the projection at all.  What it pins is the part that must NOT move: the fracture.  MEASURED, 90 deletions and the SAME 90 ELEMENTS as fast-plain, which is what same_deletion_set_as asserts; only the trajectory shifts, 508 increments against 507.  The shift is one-sided and explainable: 68 of the 90 elements fail EARLIER and none later, by at most 6.72 per cent in load fraction, because on these tetrahedra the projection onto the major principal direction is LARGER than the cube root of six volumes, and a larger L accumulates damage faster.  The reference for the width itself is not here but in test/crackband/run_cbwidth_test.sh, which checks it against hand-computable geometry, and the reason the two lengths agree so closely on this deck at all is that on the corner tetrahedron of a cube they are exactly equal - see case 5 there.  DISCLOSURE: this case runs the projection on C3D4 only, because the deck is C3D4.  The lift of the C3D4 restriction that the same switch performs is covered SEPARATELY, by hex-nonlocal-card (integral backend) and hex-gradient-card (gradient backend) - which was outside the gate when this description was first written and is not any more.  That case pins a geometric neighbour count rather than a verdict, because the two failures it guards against were both silent: a hexahedral deck ran unregularised while looking healthy. REBASELINED when the unconditional CCX_DAMAGE_TANGENT=UNSYM export was removed from run_s3rad.sh, so this case now runs the binary's DEFAULT tangent instead of a forced one. What moved is trajectory and nothing else: last_inc 508 -> 506; theta stays 1.0 exactly. The deletion set was checked element by element against the run with the export and is IDENTICAL (90 elements, same members) - that check is what makes this a rebaseline rather than a change of answer, and if it had moved the removal would have been stopped instead. Measured cost of the removal on this gate: 154 s against 179 s for the full 20 cases at -j 2, one thread per process - NOT the 37 percent the binary's banner quotes, which was measured on s3rad rather than on these decks.

cases.name: hex-nonlocal-card
cases.what: the nonlocal model proved to ENGAGE on a family that is not a linear tetrahedron, asked for on the MATERIAL CARD rather than through the environment. Both halves of that were broken until this session: the regularisation skipped every element that was not C3D4, so a hexahedral deck ran unregularised while CB1 was already letting it reach the damage law; and every guard asked ellsave, which only CCX_DAMAGE_NONLOCAL writes, so a card-only deck never entered the nonlocal block at all and looked like a healthy local run. Both failures were SILENT, which is why a count is pinned rather than a verdict: 'mean neighbours' is geometric - how many elements fall inside 2*ell - so it is exact and does not drift with the solution. If either half regresses this goes to zero. What is NOT pinned is convergence: this deck does not reach the end of its step with the internal length on, and that is a characterised limitation of the staggered scheme, not a defect - pinning it would cement it. CCX_DAMAGE_TANGENT is cleared explicitly because the rank-1 term is NOT zero on multi-point elements and makes this deck fail earlier: measured, theta=0.135 with it against 0.215 without. DISCLOSURE, added after Agent 1 fixed the divisor of this very count: this deck CANNOT see that fix. mkhex.py emits one *Element block, Type=C3D8, and nothing else - measured by generating a deck, not assumed - so every element is regularised and the two counts the banner now prints, 'N regularised of M', are equal by construction. The number pinned here was therefore right by COINCIDENCE while the divisor was wrong, and pinning the second number would add a second coincidence rather than coverage. The deck that can see it is a MIXED one - fast-plain is 2160 C3D4 against 2196 total - and no case pins it there. Deliberately not adding one: the wrong divisor moved a printed number, not an answer, and the banner now names both counts side by side, which a reader sees without a solver run. UPDATED 24.09 by Agent 1: the limitation described above was the lag of the staggered scheme, not the scheme itself. The averaged driving variable is an increment measured over the previous converged step; after a cutback it was handed out unchanged at a step up to a thousand times smaller. CCX_DAMAGE_NONLOCAL_DTSCALE (default on) hands out the lagged rate times the current step, and with it this deck reaches the end of its step: rc=0, theta=1.0, 76 increments. Convergence is therefore pinned now, because it is no longer a known limitation but the property the fix is for. RED PATH, run: CCX_DAMAGE_NONLOCAL_DTSCALE=0 stops it again at theta=0.215, rc=201, where it always stopped. Refreshing inside Newton instead (CCX_DAMAGE_NONLOCAL_INNER=1) does NOT rescue it - measured, it stops at the same theta=0.215 as with no fix at all.

cases.name: hex-gradient-card
cases.what: the IMPLICIT GRADIENT backend on hexahedra, with the internal length taken from the MATERIAL CARD. Nothing in the gate ran this backend at all before this case, which is how it carried two silent failures at once: it skipped every element that was not C3D4 - so a hexahedral deck got NO regularisation while the banner named a backend - and it read ell from the ENVIRONMENT only, so a card-only deck ran with ell=0, i.e. ebar=e, which is again no regularisation. Neither shows up as a wrong answer to look at: a run that regularises nothing converges BETTER, so any expectation on convergence or deletions would have gone GREEN on both. What is pinned is therefore GEOMETRIC and exact: packed=576 is the size of the packed conductivity, 16 hexahedra times 8*9/2=36, so it is zero if the family is skipped and wrong if the packing is; gradell=0.3 is the length the backend armed itself with, which is 0.0 if the card is not read; gradrefused=0 says no element was dropped. Measured on the merged tree. Convergence is NOT pinned: this deck does not reach the end of its step with the internal length on, the same characterised limitation of the staggered scheme that hex-nonlocal-card carries, and pinning it would cement it. ADDED after the banner and the assembly came apart: gradell is what the backend REPORTS, and the per-element length was read into ell2e and then overwritten by the global one further down the same loop, so a card-only deck ran the whole backend at ell=0 - no regularisation - while the banner printed the card's 0.3 and this case stayed green. gradrel is a FLOOR on how far the regularised field actually moved from the local one, measured at 1.7e-2 here and exactly ZERO when the length does not reach the assembly. It pins what the backend DID, not what it was asked for. CHANGED 24.09 by Agent 1, twice in one day. (1) The first change pinned rc=0 at ell=0.3 after the time-consistent lag let this deck finish; that pin is withdrawn with (2). (2) ell=0.3 is NOT RESOLVED by this deck - unit cubes, an estimated 0.9 elements within 2*ell, and the solver says so in its own warning - so the gradrel this case pinned there (1.7e-2, later 4.3e-2) was smoothing over the MESH, not over ell. The back-projection that produced it (dploc + Q(ebar - ebar0)) was retracted the same day: it passed every element mode the nodes cannot carry with factor one, and its dissipation length followed h (0.40 at h=0.25, 0.24 at h=0.125 for ell=0.5) instead of the continuum 2*sqrt(c); Bazant and Jirasek 2002, eq. 63, is the measure. The backend now interpolates ebar as Peerlings et al. 1996 do (their eq. 20) and hands an UNRESOLVED element its local value, so at ell=0.3 gradrel is exactly 0 - correct, and useless as a check. Hence ell=0.5 here: participation 4.2, resolved. gradrel is a FLOOR of 0.3: measured 0.568 with the interpolation, 0.089 on the binary before the change (7e5a596), so the retracted construction fails it - that is the red path, run. Convergence is again NOT pinned, and for a physical reason: at ell=0.5 the dissipation length 2*ell=1 is a quarter of this specimen, damage spreads through all of it, and all 16 elements stand at D=1 by theta=0.62 (none is deleted), after which nothing carries load and the run stops with rc=201. That is the end of the problem on a specimen this short against its internal length - Pijaudier-Cabot and Bazant 1987 note the same for a beam short against l - not a failure of the scheme: with CCX_DAMAGE_VISCOSITY=1e-3 the same deck runs to theta=1.0.

cases.name: cross-integral-lag
cases.what: the TIME-CONSISTENT LAG of the staggered nonlocal scheme. The averaged driving variable is rebuilt once per converged increment and read on every Newton iteration of the next one; it is an INCREMENT, so after a cutback the damage law used to receive a full previous step's increment at a step up to a thousand times smaller, and no cutback could remove the residual that made. CCX_DAMAGE_NONLOCAL_DTSCALE (on by default) hands out the lagged rate times the current step instead. This arm - the notched bar of mkcross.py, INTEGRAL backend at l=0.375 - is the one Agent 2 found dying deterministically between two passing lengths: with the switch set to 0 it stops at theta=0.3675, rc=201, the wall tools/wallclass.py classifies as carried-in (first residual 17.5 at dt=1e-2, 26.3 at dt=1e-5); with it on it runs to the end of the step, rc=0, 124 increments, 276 iterations, 9 deletions. RED PATH, run: CCX_DAMAGE_NONLOCAL_DTSCALE=0 in the environment turns this case red on rc. Deletions are NOT pinned - the count follows the trajectory, and what the case is for is that the step can be finished at all. CCX_DAMAGE_NLWIDTH=0 is pinned in the env since 24.09, when the dissipation-length width became the default: with it this arm finishes even with the lag unscaled, so the case would stop seeing the lag - the configuration it pins is the one the lag killed. The GRADIENT arm on the same bar is cross-gradient-bp.

cases.name: cross-gradient-bp
cases.what: the GRADIENT backend's back-projection, on the arm it used to kill: the notched bar of mkcross.py at ell=0.5 (h=0.25, participation well above two), everything else as cross-integral-lag. Until 24.09 the backend returned dploc + Q(ebar - ebar0) per element, to make ell -> 0 reduce to the local model exactly. It did, and at every other ell it passed each element mode the nodes cannot carry with factor one - 47 of 144 on this mesh, 1596 of 2160 on test/fast - so two tetrahedra of one cross-section could soften alone: before the wall D ranged 0.14 to 0.86 inside one slice of a bar in uniaxial tension, the tangent went near singular, and the first Newton correction hit its cap at every step size down to 1e-5. Its dissipation length (Bazant and Jirasek 2002, eq. 63) followed the mesh, 0.40 at h=0.25 and 0.24 at h=0.125, instead of ell. The backend now interpolates ebar as Peerlings et al. 1996 do (eq. 20) and hands an unresolved element its local value. Measured: rc=0, theta=1.0, 118 increments, 271 iterations, 14 deletions; full refresh inside Newton had needed 601 iterations to get past the same wall. RED PATH, run: the binary before the change (7e5a596) stops at theta=0.2575, rc=201. Deletions are not pinned.

cases.name: cross-separation-end
cases.what: the END of a regularised fracture: the notched bar of run_nlobjectivity.sh at h=0.125, INTEGRAL backend, ell=0.5. It used to stop with rc=201 at theta=0.139 and was the one arm missing from the objectivity sweep. It is not a scheme failure: the end force is 0.155 against a peak of 373.6 (0.04 per cent), the coarser meshes carry 0.4 and 0.7 per cent at the same theta, and at the rollbacks of inc 28 and 30 [FRACTURE SEPARATION] finds the grips joined only by 24 bulk elements at D>=0.999 - broken by the damage law, held by the viscous lag Dvis alone (a regularisation, Gao and Bower 2004). The final stop comes at inc 31 on an ordinary Newton failure after every rescue level, which is why the separation flag is sticky: damage never decreases. The step now ends as a completed fracture, rc=0. RED PATH, run: the binary before the change (e6329a7) returns rc=201 here. theta is not pinned - it follows the trajectory; log_has pins why the run ended.

log_has: joined only by material the damage law has broken
